newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end lower, dragged down by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end lower, dragged down by Wall St.

text.p: Madrid stocks lost early gains on Wednesday to close down, dragged lower by a weak opening on Wall Street. Dealers said Spanish stocks remained vulnerable and the short-term outlook would be determined by the U.S. market.
The general index ended 1.11 points lower, or 0.24 percent, to 464.03, while the blue chip Ibex-35 index ended down 16.12 points, or 0.3 percent, to 5,310.42.
"This slide has made things worse, but the underlying tone was already negative," a dealer in Madrid said.
Traders expected stocks to tread water on Thursday and Friday, before the release of March U.S. jobless data which is likely to give some hints about the future economic perspective.
Telefonica ended 45 pesetas down at 3,200 pesetas, after heavy trade, while Repsol outperformed the market adding 10 to 5,840 pesetas.
Amid banking stocks, both Banesto and Popular bucked the trend adding gains. Banesto gained 5 pesetas to 1,095, while Popular gained 100 to 25,140 pesetas.
